dangerous_cpts.main_problem: A repeated failure-associated parameter favors Execution_Integrity=Normal when Program_Anomaly=Yes and both local deviation aggregators are No. This semantically suppresses anomaly propagation at a key bottleneck directly upstream of Root_Causes.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This parameter is independently flagged as suspicious on multiple suspicious paths and directly reinforces a normal execution conclusion despite Program_Anomaly=Yes. Reducing it should allow anomaly evidence to propagate more appropriately to Root_Causes.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The response-side deviation aggregator appears semantically inverted for the all-Found parent configuration, assigning very high probability to Deviation_in_Response=No when all response-chain expected deviations are present. Because this node feeds Execution_Integrity directly, the parameter can suppress valid local anomaly evidence.

suspicious_parameters.justification: Although activated in both failures and successes, the semantic mismatch is severe: all five response-side LPTN parents being Found should not strongly imply no response deviation. A decrease is well supported because this parameter likely blocks evidence before it reaches Execution_Integrity.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The dispatch-side deviation aggregator strongly favors Deviation_in_Dispatch=No when all dispatch-chain expected deviations are Found, which conflicts with its intended aggregation semantics. This can directly suppress dispatch-side evidence before it influences Execution_Integrity and Root_Causes.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This parameter is semantically inverted and moderately failure-skewed, making it a strong refinement target. Lowering this probability should help dispatch-side deviations propagate instead of being suppressed.

overall_summary: The best-supported refinement space is concentrated in three HIGH-risk CPTs that suppress anomaly propagation at key aggregation stages. Network_Manipulation is not included because its flagged parameters are either only uncertain or semantically plausible, whereas the selected CPTs show stronger structural and semantic evidence of harmful probability assignments.
